items.title: Technical Program Manager, Cloud
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE We are seeking experienced and highly motivated Technical Program Managers (TPMs) to join our Cloud Infrastructure organization and drive the delivery of complex, high-impact infrastructure programs. As Mistral continues to scale its AI compute infrastructure, bringing new capacity online quickly and reliably is critical to our success. This involves not only deploying physical infrastructure but also coordinating the engineering efforts required to make that infrastructure fully operational. In this role, you will work at the intersection of cloud engineering, software infrastructure, and data center deployments, ensuring seamless execution across multiple technical teams. You will coordinate programs involving networking, storage, Kubernetes, fleet management, and infrastructure operations, working closely with engineering teams to manage dependencies, anticipate risks, and accelerate the deployment of production-ready compute capacity. The TPM role spans several critical areas of program management: Cloud Infrastructure Deployment – Coordinate the software deployment and bring-up of new compute infrastructure, ensuring smooth transitions from physical data center deployment to fully operational cloud environments. Technical Program Management – Plan, execute, and oversee complex infrastructure programs involving multiple engineering teams, managing dependencies, timelines, and technical risks to ensure successful delivery. Cross-Functional Engineering Coordination – Work closely with Cloud Engineering, Data Center Infrastructure, Networking, Storage, Kubernetes, and Fleet teams to align priorities, resolve blockers, and drive execution. Engineering Operations & Process Improvement – Identify opportunities to streamline infrastructure deployment processes, improve coordination, and introduce scalable, lightweight workflows that accelerate delivery. LOCATION & OFFICE POLICY The position is based in our Paris HQ offices and we encourage going to the office as much as we can (at least 3 days per week) to create bonds and smooth communication. Our remote policy aims to provide flexibility, improve work-life balance and increase productivity. Each manager can decide the amount of days worked remotely based on autonomy and a specific context (e.g. more flexibility can occur during summer). In any case, employees are expected to maintain regular communication with their teams and be available during core working hours. WHAT YOU WILL DO Program Management — Lead and coordinate complex cloud infrastructure programs, from physical infrastructure handover through software deployment and production readiness. Infrastructure Deployment — Oversee the software bring-up of newly deployed compute infrastructure, coordinating engineering teams responsible for networking, storage, Kubernetes, fleet delivery, and infrastructure health. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Work closely with Cloud Engineering, Data Center Infrastructure, and other technical teams to ensure alignment across deployment activities, technical dependencies, and operational priorities. Project Delivery — Define and track project milestones, timelines, and resources. Anticipate blockers, coordinate technical dependencies, and ensure infrastructure is brought into production efficiently and reliably. Process Improvement — Continuously identify opportunities to improve deployment workflows, reduce time to production, and establish scalable processes that support our growing infrastructure needs. Stakeholder Management — Maintain clear communication with engineering teams, technical leads, and leadership, providing visibility into program progress, risks, and key decisions. Risk Management — Proactively identify technical and operational risks, develop mitigation strategies, and drive the resolution of critical issues that could delay infrastructure availability. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - You hold a degree in a relevant scientific or technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline). - You have at least 4 years of relevant experience managing technical programs, preferably in cloud infrastructure, software infrastructure, data centers, GPU computing, hosting, or related environments. - You have proven experience coordinating complex technical projects involving multiple engineering teams and interdependent workstreams. - You have a strong understanding of infrastructure deployment processes and the technical challenges involved in bringing systems into production. - You have excellent project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple complex programs and drive execution in fast-paced environments. - You thrive in cross-functional collaboration and can effectively communicate with engineers, technical leads, and senior stakeholders. - You are highly organized and know how to manage cross-team dependencies, anticipate blockers, and keep projects moving forward. - You are a proactive problem-solver with a continuous improvement mindset, comfortable navigating ambiguity and taking ownership. Ideally, you have: - Experience managing cloud infrastructure or large-scale data center deployment programs. - A background in cloud engineering, software infrastructure, platform engineering, or a related technical field. - Familiarity with Kubernetes, networking, storage systems, distributed systems, or infrastructure automation. - Experience working on GPU infrastructure, HPC environments, or large-scale compute deployments. - Experience coordinating projects involving both physical infrastructure and software engineering teams. - Previous experience as a Software Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, SRE, or Technical Program Manager. - Already worked in an AI company or on large-scale AI infrastructure projects. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.title: Sr. Security Risk Management Analyst
items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Kraken’s world-class Security Team is growing. As we continue to scale and mature our information technology controls program, we are seeking a senior professional with a strong background in risk management to help build and operate a program designed for enterprise scale. Kraken is seeking a Senior Risk Analyst to join the Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (SecGRC) team. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Security Risk Management, this role is a key contributor to the execution and maturation of Kraken's Security Risk Management program. You'll conduct rigorous risk assessments, produce high-quality analysis, and help build the operational infrastructure that makes the program run — all in close partnership with program leadership. This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting impact both within Kraken and across the broader industry. The ideal candidate is deeply analytical, process-minded, and energized by turning ambiguous risk signals into clear, repeatable, and scalable workflows. Entrepreneurial spirit and comfort with iterating quickly is a must. This is a fully remote role. THE OPPORTUNITY - Execute security risk assessments end-to-end — scoping, data gathering, analysis, findings documentation, and communicating results to stakeholders — in alignment with program methodology set by leadership - Support the development and continuous refinement of risk assessment templates, workflows, and process guides that make the program consistent and scalable - Maintain risk registers and ensure identified risks are tracked accurately and progressing through mitigation, remediation, or acceptance workflows - Assist in building and maintaining Key Risk Indicators (KRI) tracking and risk reporting outputs, translating raw data into clear, well-structured deliverables for review by senior leadership - Partner with technical teams including Vulnerability Management, Application Security, and Blue Team to gather risk-relevant data and incorporate operational findings into assessment work - Identify opportunities to streamline and automate risk processes and bring those recommendations to program leadership for prioritization - Contribute to the documentation and upkeep of risk program standards, procedures, and guidance materials - Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Compliance, Internal Audit, Engineering, and Legal to ensure risk findings are well-contextualized and properly actioned - Support audit preparedness activities and risk-related reporting as directed by program leadership WHAT YOU BRING - 5+ years of experience in information security risk management, cybersecurity governance, or GRC - Hands-on experience conducting risk assessments and owning findings documentation — not just supporting assessments, but running them - Strong working knowledge of risk management frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27005, PCI DSS, or DoCRA - Demonstrated ability to build repeatable processes — you've taken something ad hoc and made it structured and scalable - Strong data analysis skills; able to clean, interpret, and present risk data clearly and accurately - Experience contributing to KRI tracking and risk reporting for internal stakeholder audiences - Familiarity with GRC tools such as AuditBoard, Archer, OneTrust, or ServiceNow GRC - Proficient in Google Workspace; SQL and/or Tableau experience a strong plus - Excellent written communication — your deliverables are clear, well-organized, and don't require heavy editing - Self-directed and comfortable operating in ambiguity; you take direction well and run with it - Bachelor's degree or above in IT, Cybersecurity, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field - CISM, CRISC, or ISO 27001 credentials a plus; experience in fintech or regulated industries preferred Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. items.title: Security GRC Analyst, Mergers & Acquisitions
items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program. Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner. This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done. THE OPPORTUNITY - Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise - Map the acquired company's existing controls to Payward's control framework, and identify gaps against the external frameworks the entity falls under once in scope - Score control maturity at the entity level and document the basis for each score - Define remediation milestones that are achievable for the acquired team's size and maturity, sequenced by risk reduction rather than by framework order - Track milestones to closure and report status to Security GRC leadership and the M&A Technology Team - Recommend the endpoint for each entity: full migration onto Payward platforms, or uplift to a maturity level the central program can absorb - Load acquired-entity risks into the enterprise risk register and keep them current - Prepare acquired entities for inclusion in external audit scope, including evidence collection and walkthrough support - Act as the Security GRC point of contact for acquired-entity leadership, finance, and internal audit - Maintain policy coverage for acquired entities, including building entity-specific policy libraries where the parent policy set does not apply cleanly - Feed recurring findings back into the diligence process, so later deals are assessed against known patterns - Document the onboarding process so that it is repeatable and not dependent on one person WHAT WILL YOU DO - Target Assessment - Review target security posture during diligence: control environment, identity and access management, infrastructure, third-party dependencies, and prior audit or examination history - Produce a written assessment of each target against the Payward security baseline, separating the risks that matter to the deal from those that matter to steady-state operations - Give the M&A Technology Team and deal sponsors a clear read on what integration will cost in control remediation terms - Control Mapping and Framework Onboarding - Map acquired controls to Payward's framework and to the external frameworks the entity becomes subject to - Identify which parent-company controls extend to the entity as they are, which need an entity-specific variant, and which have no equivalent at all - Build the entity's policy library where the parent policy set does not cover it - Remediation and Milestones - Set milestones the acquired team can meet, each with a date, an owner, and a stated risk reduction - Sequence work so that the highest-risk gaps close first rather than the easiest ones - Run the cadence for tracking remediation and escalating overdue or material risks Prepare proposed risk acceptances, including the rationale and compensating controls, and present them to leadership for decision - Program Integration - Prepare entities for external audit inclusion and support fieldwork - Keep acquired-entity risk visible in the enterprise risk register and in Security GRC reporting - Hand each entity over to central GRC coverage once its maturity supports it, with the handover documented - Integrate 3rd parties and vendors into Payward WHAT YOU BRING - 5-7+ years in security governance, IT risk, or compliance, including regulated financial services, fintech, or virtual asset environments - Direct experience onboarding an acquired company into an existing controls or compliance program. This is the core of the role - Working knowledge of SOX/ICFR IT general controls and what external auditors accept as evidence - Experience with at least two of ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI DSS, including mapping controls across frameworks - Ability to assess control maturity and set remediation plans the receiving team completes, including teams below Payward's maturity level - Hands-on delivery: you write the scope, collect the evidence, and close gaps yourself when needed - Sound judgment on priorities with incomplete information, and the sense to escalate decisions that need leadership - Ability to build working relationships with control owners in IAM, infrastructure, and engineering - Ability to translate control gaps into risk language that deal teams and executives can act on - Strong project management across cross-functional, distributed teams - Preferred - CISA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer - M&A or post-merger technology integration experience - Familiarity with PKM WHY THIS ROLE - You will own a domain end to end rather than supporting someone else's.
